casper_customer: Hey team — around 08:45 PDT our Dedicated cluster started returning intermittent 429s and a bunch of high-latency responses. Customer-facing timeouts. We're seeing a big jump in token usage & a billing alert came in. Can you advise?

jessica_cs: Sorry you're hitting this, casper. Can you paste the cluster id + workspace id and an example request/response? Also which model + region?

casper_customer: cluster: dc-us-west-2-17, ws: ws-9012, model: rwd/gptx-large, region: us-west-2. Example response: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` and body: `{\"error\":\"admission_rejected\",\"reason\":\"burst_credits_exhausted\"}`

oncall-bot: ALERT: AdmissionControlHighRejections for dc-us-west-2-17 — 429 rate > 5% over 3m — triggered at 2026-03-17T08:46:02Z

raj_sre: pulling admission_controller logs now. I see repeated lines like: `admission_controller: reject req_id=abc123 reason=burst_credits_exhausted headroom=0 queued=42 tokens_requested=1200` — burst_credits went to 0 at 08:46:12.

alex_runtime: Looks like autoscaler didn't add GPUs fast enough. K8s events show `ProvisioningFailed: GCE quota limit` for the nodepool bound to that dedicated cluster. So autoscale policy attempted to scale but cloud quota blocked new nodes.

sam_support: Billing bot shows a token burn spike coinciding with the rejection window. billing-bot, can you paste the exact usage delta?

billing-bot: usage_snapshot: {"ws":"ws-9012","period_start":"2026-03-17T08:40:00Z","period_end":"2026-03-17T08:50:00Z","tokens":"+12,400,000"} — burst_credits before spike: 150k tokens, after: 0.

jessica_cs: Summary: rapid client traffic (large prompts) burned burst credits -> admission controller started rejecting -> autoscaler couldn't add capacity due to cloud quota -> persisted rejections and latency.

casper_customer: Ugh. We didn't intentionally spike — one worker job retried aggressively after timeouts. How do we reproduce to test the fix?

raj_sre: Repro steps (small, safe): run a moderate parallel load that approximates their peak. Example script: 
```
TOKEN=REDACTED
for i in $(seq 1 150); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd/gptx-large","input":"'"'$(python -c "print('a'*800)" )'"'"}' &
done
wait
```
Expect to see a subset return 429 with the `admission_rejected` reason when burst credits hit zero.

alex_runtime: Short-term mitigation we can apply now: 1) temporarily increase burst credit allocation for ws-9012 by +300k (manual top-up) 2) set admission policy to allow emergency headroom for 2m: `admission.override(ws-9012, window=120s)` 3) failover some traffic to a lower-cost/easier-to-serve model (rwd/gptx-medium) via routing rule.

sam_support: I'm going to request the manual top-up and the admission override now. @raj_sre can you patch a routing rule to send low-priority requests to the fallback model?

raj_sre: On it. Creating a canary route for calls with header `x-priority: low` -> rwd/gptx-medium. Also adding a temporary admission alert to notify sooner.

casper_customer: Appreciate it. Long-term, what's the recommended fix?

jessica_cs: Recommendations: 1) add client-side rate limiter + exponential backoff on your worker job to avoid retry storms 2) increase committed reserved capacity or configured headroom for predictable peaks 3) pre-warm autoscaler quotas with cloud provider (request quota increases) 4) monitor `burst_credit_balance` metric and auto-topup rules for critical workspaces.

alex_runtime: Also consider prompt shaping (reduce input length) or model quantization to cut tokens per request. For dedicated customers, we can set a higher admission headroom threshold in the cluster profile.

casper_customer: For the immediate window, can you confirm when the manual top-up and override are done?

sam_support: Top-up requested (INC-2026-7782). Cloud quota request submitted to provider as well. Admission override applied at 08:47:20Z — you should see rejections subside.

billing-bot: Note: manual top-up will be invoiced as a one-time adjustment to your next invoice. Details in the support ticket.

oncall-bot: RESOLVED ALERT: AdmissionControlHighRejections for dc-us-west-2-17 — rejections dropped below threshold at 2026-03-17T08:48:40Z

casper_customer: I'm seeing the 429s drop. Latency looks better. Thanks for the fast triage. We'll roll back the aggressive retries and implement backoff.

jessica_cs: Great — leaving this thread open until we've verified stable for 24h and cloud quota is approved. I'll add remediation items to the ticket and a follow-up for capacity planning. :thumbsup:
